name: netdust-core
description: 0.7.0: the worktable skill — a planned feature mirrored into Studio over the worktable MCP: the werkpakket by repo and branch, each plan.md `### Task N` as a Taak row keyed by its stap label, every stop a state change (bezig · geblokkeerd · gedaan · overgeslagen), the werkpakket written last so its writer recounts voortgang; the plan stays the truth, a box without worktable skips and the next session catches up, never a reason to wait or to reach the engine another way. 0.6.0: hc-orchestration replaces herdr-orchestration (hc-flow spec) — role templates coder, reviewer and sparring in hc-templates/, installed by bin/hc-templates; the pair recipe on hc (the coder from its template with --outlive-parent, labelled into the reviewer's space); no default worktree, urgent work under ~/.herdr/worktrees; watching by hc wait and hc events; the observer reference; an agent never starts the user's core. Evals S1–S6, tests/run.sh with scratch-core tests. 0.5.4: the pair recipe in herdr-orchestration — the thinker turns reviewer at the plan approval and starts a coder session (Role: coder) in the feature's own worktree, in the same permission mode; pre-flight rulings, review at checkpoints with one fix request per finding, the Close split, and a restart from the branch, the plan and the coder's ledger. Scenario 6 (H29–H38). 0.5.3: docs follow the current flow — netdust-gates owns the policy and hooks, netdust-devops the branches and deploy; the Close runs gate → review → fix → shakeout → promote; feature artifacts live in specs/<feature>/. 0.5.2: RULES.md speaks the seven-verb simple flow — feature/hotfix from production, staging rebuilt by promote/unpromote, ship's three origin-read equalities and its own inline gate. 0.5.1: herdr-orchestration re-anchored on herdr 0.9.0 — saved machines, client-only updates, grouped workspace close, stalled prompts. 0.5.0: devops moved out — the branch flow, make verbs, deploy gate/ledger and site.yml schema now live in netdust-devops; the dev-stack skill and the /deploy command are gone from here. Netdust business + ops + content core: content/marketing skills (brand-voice, marketing, market-research), the design-builder skill, the research skill, server-lifecycle skills (ploi, secure-server), herdr-orchestration, /memory-audit + /pattern-miner, and the ploi MCP. NOT a coding harness — that is netdust-gates. Stack-agnostic.
